name: NAVSIM
modality: End-to-end driving policy receives real sensor data + ego state from OpenScene/nuPlan; outputs a trajectory; scored by PDM Score (PDMS) computed by non-reactive BEV unrolling over a 4 s horizon at 10 Hz (collision, drivable area, ego progress, TTC, comfort).
what_it_measures: Whether open-loop-style evaluation on real logs can predict closed-loop driving quality; ranks vision-based end-to-end planners on collision/progress/comfort subscores.
size: navtrain 103k samples, navtest 12k samples (after filtering trivial scenes)
reported_metrics: PDMS shows higher Spearman correlation with nuPlan closed-loop score than displacement errors; CVPR 2024 challenge: 143 teams, 463 submissions; TransFuser-style methods match UniAD.
cost_evidence: Non-reactive BEV simulation, no sensor rendering; designed to be cheap enough for large-scale benchmarking (thousands of scenes per evaluation).
validity_evidence: Correlation of PDMS with nuPlan closed-loop score reported in-paper; independent 2026 study (arXiv 2605.00066, not Pavone) finds PDMS strongly but non-monotonically correlated with closed-loop Bench2Drive and Spearman 0.90 for a 3-metric variant.
bibtex: @inproceedings{dauner2024navsim, title={NAVSIM: Data-Driven Non-Reactive Autonomous Vehicle Simulation and Benchmarking}, author={Dauner, Daniel and Hallgarten, Marcel and Li, Tianyu and Weng, Xinshuo and Huang, Zhiyu and Yang, Zetong and Li, Hongyang and Gilitschenski, Igor and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Geiger, Andreas and Chitta, Kashyap}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)}, volume={37}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15349}}
notes: Pavone is a co-author (NVIDIA). Core citation for cheap-proxy-vs-closed-loop validity.

name: Pseudo-Simulation (NAVSIM v2)
modality: Planner is evaluated on real logs augmented with 3D-Gaussian-Splatting synthetic observations (perturbed position/heading/speed); two-stage rollout; scored by Extended PDM Score (EPDMS, nine subscores with multiplicative rule penalties) with proximity-based weighting of synthetic views.
what_it_measures: Error recovery and causal-confusion robustness of end-to-end planners without interactive simulation; correlation with closed-loop outcomes.
size: navhard: 450 Stage-1 and 5462 Stage-2 observations (~12 synthetic views per real observation); public leaderboard
reported_metrics: Pearson r=0.89 (R^2=0.8) with closed-loop nuPlan results vs R^2=0.7 for best open-loop; 6x fewer environment interactions than closed-loop (13 vs 80 planner inferences per scenario).
cost_evidence: Neural rendering ~1-2 GPU-hours per scene for synthetic views (one-off, offline); evaluation itself needs 13 planner calls per scenario.
validity_evidence: R^2=0.8 vs closed-loop simulation reported; no correlation to real-world crash outcomes.
bibtex: @inproceedings{cao2025pseudosim, title={Pseudo-Simulation for Autonomous Driving}, author={Cao, Wei and Hallgarten, Marcel and Li, Tianyu and Dauner, Daniel and Gu, Xunjiang and Wang, Caojun and Miron, Yakov and Aiello, Marco and Li, Hongyang and Gilitschenski, Igor and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Geiger, Andreas and Chitta, Kashyap}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04218}}
notes: Direct evidence on cost-vs-fidelity trade-off of evaluation paradigms; Pavone co-author.

name: Sim2Val
modality: Paired measurements of the same scenario on a cheap platform (simulator / open-loop playback) and the expensive target platform (closed-loop or real vehicle); real-world metric mean estimated with control variates.
what_it_measures: How many real-world test samples are needed for a confidence bound on a safety/performance metric when correlated cheap proxies exist; variance reduction of the estimator.
size: nuPlan: 565 real + 1320 surrogate samples; real AV: 138 intersection / 75 curve events paired with 781 / 423 neural-reconstruction sim runs; quadruped: 200 real + 400 sim
reported_metrics: Variance reduction 22-35% (nuPlan ADE), 82.9% (real AV closest-distance), 5.9% (quadruped, rho=0.07); 51% fewer paired samples for same CI in one domain; sim-real correlation rho>0.9 for AV logs vs 0.07 for quadruped.
cost_evidence: Cost ratios between platforms formalised (budget allocation in appendix); real AV logs and quadruped hardware used; no dollar figures.
validity_evidence: Method's benefit is itself a function of measured sim-to-real correlation; reports rho per platform.
bibtex: @inproceedings{luo2025sim2val, title={Sim2Val: Leveraging Correlation Across Test Platforms for Variance-Reduced Metric Estimation}, author={Luo, Rachel and Yang, Heng and Watson, Michael and Sharma, Apoorva and Veer, Sushant and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20553}}
notes: Closest existing work to a value-of-information framing of evaluation cost; must-cite.

name: X4Val
modality: Non-paired heterogeneous evaluation data (simulation, older policy logs, other regions) embedded with DINO features; learned predictor of real-world metric used as a control variate for the target policy's real-world evaluation.
what_it_measures: Variance-reduced estimation of real-world policy metrics when only unpaired auxiliary data exists (e.g. geographic transfer US to Germany, iterative policy versions).
size: Driving: 200 paired target samples plus 5x1000 samples from earlier policies and 86,848 scenario-only samples; manipulation: 5000 ManiSkill rollouts + 100 real Franka rollouts
reported_metrics: Up to 38.4% variance reduction (iterative development), 15-20% (geographic transfer); consistent reduction on Franka block stacking.
cost_evidence: Real Franka Panda rollouts (100) vs 5000 sim rollouts; NVIDIA PhysicalAI-AV dataset; no hours or dollars stated.
validity_evidence: Reports variance reduction against Monte Carlo on real data; no external ground truth on safety outcomes.
bibtex: @article{luo2026x4val, title={X4Val: Learning Neural Surrogates for Variance-Reduced Policy Evaluation}, author={Luo, Rachel and Watson, Michael and Sharma, Apoorva and Yang, Heng and Qi, Han and Schmerling, Edward and Veer, Sushant and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.05159}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05159}}
notes: Follow-up to Sim2Val; preprint.

name: Coverage-Aware Active Evaluation (paired systems)
modality: Cheap proxy system (open-loop playback, lower-fidelity sim, related policy) sampled densely; target system (closed-loop sim, second sim, real Unitree Go2, real KITTI) evaluated under a small budget; scenario selection via residual-corrected risk predictor plus support-aware mutual information.
what_it_measures: Number and diversity of severe target-system failures found under a fixed test budget when proxy evaluations are available.
size: Budgets: nuPlan 170 target evals, SIMPLER 70, quadruped 30 real trials; KITTI perception transfer
reported_metrics: Up to 2x more failures discovered than random and active-learning baselines, including severe/diverse failures missed by baselines.
cost_evidence: Explicit small target budgets (30-170 evaluations) with proxy evaluations treated as cheap; real Unitree Go2 hardware.
validity_evidence: Failures found on real hardware and real KITTI data, not just sim; no predictive validity vs field incidents.
bibtex: @article{parashar2026coverage, title={Coverage Aware Active Evaluation for Failure Discovery with Paired Systems}, author={Parashar, Anjali and Luo, Rachel and Sharma, Apoorva and Veer, Sushant and Schmerling, Edward and Sobolewski, Carson and Yu, Mingxin and Fan, Chuchu and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.13719}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13719}}
notes: Directly about allocating limited real-world test budget; preprint.

name: StressDream
modality: Action-conditioned video world model (Vista for driving, Ctrl-World for DROID manipulation); initial diffusion noise optimised with a VLM semantic objective plus plausibility objective to steer imagined futures toward text-specified failures; policy scored by whether plausible steered futures contain the failure.
what_it_measures: Whether steered world-model imaginations can surface rare high-impact failures of a policy with few samples, and whether that signal improves policies.
size: Driving: 100 image-action-text pairs in 8 safety-critical categories + 200 imminent-collision examples; manipulation: 100 failure trajectories over 6 tasks
reported_metrics: Failure recall on manipulation 54% (random sampling) to 94% (StressDream); pi0.5 fine-tuning success 39% to 71%.
cost_evidence: World-model imaginations take several minutes each; noise optimisation adds cost but replaces exhaustive sampling.
validity_evidence: Failure detection recall vs ground-truth failure trajectories; no real-world closed-loop validation of imagined failures.
bibtex: @article{seo2026stressdream, title={StressDream: Steering Video World Models for Robust Policy Evaluation and Improvement}, author={Seo, Junwon and Veer, Sushant and Tian, Ran and Ding, Wenhao and Sharma, Apoorva and Leung, Karen and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco and Bajcsy, Andrea}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.00267}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00267}}
notes: Co-authored with Andrea Bajcsy (also a workshop-relevant speaker). World-model-based evaluation.

name: Swiss Re / Stanford ADAS proving-ground assessment
modality: Physical vehicles (12 production models MY2022-23 + 1 prototype) driven on a Euro NCAP-accredited proving ground through safety-critical scenarios selected from insurer accident databases; scored by predicted real-world collision-frequency and impact-energy reduction weighted by scenario relevance; realism metric on tested scenarios.
what_it_measures: Relative real-world safety benefit of collision-prevention systems across vehicles; realism of the scenario protocol.
size: 13 vehicles; average 81 tests per vehicle (range 41-161; 18-72% of full matrix); 8-month campaign
reported_metrics: All tested scenarios score as highly realistic (mean realism 0.0024, sd 0.0012 on a nondimensional scale); pre-release prototype outperforms production vehicles in most scenarios.
cost_evidence: Eight-month track campaign at an accredited proving ground in Germany with 13 vehicles; roughly 1000 physical test runs; insurer-funded.
validity_evidence: Scoring explicitly ties to predicted real-world collision frequency; realism metric validates scenario plausibility; no post-hoc comparison to field claims yet.
bibtex: @article{dilillo2024adas, title={Performance assessment of ADAS in a representative subset of critical traffic situations}, author={Di Lillo, Luigi and Triscari, Andrea and Zhou, Xilin and Dyro, Robert and Li, Ruolin and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.16942}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16942}}
notes: Rare example of a costly physical safety evaluation with explicit run counts; strong cost anchor.

name: Realistic Extreme Behavior Generation for AV Testing
modality: Collision-free Waymo Open / nuScenes scenes; adversary trajectories perturbed in the parameter space of a learned behaviour model (MTR, Trajectron++) under a data-alignment realism constraint; counterfactual collisions clustered into a test suite; target AV policy run against them.
what_it_measures: Interpretable failure modes of an AV collision-avoidance policy under realistic adversarial counterfactual collisions.
reported_metrics: Baseline reactive policy: 100% response to high-speed chasing/side crashes, 55-59% no-response for low-speed lateral crashes.
cost_evidence: Runs on public datasets and learned predictors; no hardware.
validity_evidence: Realism enforced via data-alignment in model parameter space; no real-crash validation.
bibtex: @inproceedings{dyro2024extreme, title={Realistic Extreme Behavior Generation for Improved AV Testing}, author={Dyro, Robert and Foutter, Matthew and Li, Ruolin and Di Lillo, Luigi and Schmerling, Edward and Zhou, Xilin and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10669}}
notes: ICRA 2025 per ASL page.

name: Surprise Potential (interactive scenario mining)
modality: Driving logs (nuScenes) scored by the ego vehicle's surprise potential on other agents (distribution-shift between prediction with and without ego); validated against a reward model trained on human pairwise interactivity preferences; planners evaluated on curated buckets.
what_it_measures: Which logged scenarios are interactive enough to be worth including in an AV benchmark; alignment with human judgement of interactivity.
size: nuScenes; 5 annotators x 1000 pairwise labels (~5000) for reward model
reported_metrics: Correlation >0.82 with human-aligned reward; 86% pairwise ranking accuracy; TTC decreases monotonically with surprise bucket.
cost_evidence: ~5000 human pairwise labels; otherwise offline computation.
validity_evidence: Human-preference agreement 0.82; downstream planner TTC trend confirms difficulty.
bibtex: @article{ding2025surprise, title={Surprise Potential as a Measure of Interactivity in Driving Scenarios}, author={Ding, Wenhao and Veer, Sushant and Leung, Karen and Cao, Yulong and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.05677}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05677}}
notes: Scenario-curation metric for evaluation; directly about making evaluations informative.

name: CrashTwin (physics-grounded world-model benchmark)
modality: Video world models prompted with multi-agent collision scenes; rollouts reconstructed to 3D kinematics with a calibration-free pipeline; scored on spatio-temporal consistency, momentum/kinetic-energy conservation residuals and world-dynamics integrity.
what_it_measures: Physical trustworthiness of generative world models used as AV simulators in collision scenarios.
size: 25.6K synthetic (CARLA) + 12.6K real collision sequences; eval sets of 300+44 and 100+16
reported_metrics: All models (Wan, Cosmos-Predict2, Veo 3.1, Seedance etc.) show high momentum/energy residuals (~0.89 vs ground truth 0.31; post-training 0.65); visual quality masks physics violations.
cost_evidence: API-constrained proprietary models needed a mini eval set; otherwise compute unspecified.
validity_evidence: Human evaluation: physics metrics align better with human realism preference than visual-quality proxies.
bibtex: @article{chen2026crashtwin, title={A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Multi-Agent Dynamics in World Models}, author={Chen, Nuo and Liu, Lulin and Li, Zihao and Zeng, Ziyao and Zhu, Zihao and Cong, Wenyan and Hong, Junyuan and Yang, Yunhao and Tu, Zhengzhong and Wang, Yan and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Wang, Zhangyang and Zhou, Yang and Fan, Zhiwen}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.28757}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28757}}
notes: Evaluates the simulator, not the AV; relevant to world-models-for-validation theme.

name: AccidentBench
modality: Multimodal LLMs answer human-annotated QA about accident videos (vehicle, air, water); scored by accuracy across temporal/spatial/intent tasks and difficulty levels.
what_it_measures: Safety-critical video understanding and reasoning of foundation models in accident scenarios.
size: ~2000 videos, >19,000 QA pairs (~6300 per difficulty level); 83% vehicle accidents
reported_metrics: GPT-5 37.3% and Gemini 2.5 Pro 31.1% on hard vehicle tasks; ~18% on hardest/longest tasks.
cost_evidence: Human annotation of >19k QA pairs; cost not stated.
validity_evidence: Human-annotated ground truth; no link to closed-loop driving safety.
bibtex: @article{gu2025accidentbench, title={AccidentBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning in Vehicle Accidents and Beyond}, author={Gu, Shangding and Wang, Xiaohan and Ying, Donghao and Zhao, Haoyu and Yang, Runing and Jin, Ming and Li, Boyi and Pavone, Marco and Yeung-Levy, Serena and Wang, Jun and Song, Dawn and Spanos, Costas}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.26636}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26636}}
notes: Pavone is one of 12 authors; benchmark tests VLMs rather than a control stack.

name: SafeVL (VLM driving-safety evaluator)
modality: Driving video fed to a VLM with object-centric chain-of-thought; outputs collision-prone / safe classification; trained with counterfactual unsafe-scenario generation; tested on Nexar collision dataset and as a critic inside UniAD on NeuroNCAP.
what_it_measures: Whether a VLM can serve as a learned safety evaluator of driving scenes and reduce closed-loop collisions when used as a critic.
size: Nexar collision dataset (size not stated); NeuroNCAP closed-loop benchmark
reported_metrics: 76% zero-shot accuracy on Nexar (+20% over prior); 8% collision-rate reduction on NeuroNCAP when integrated with UniAD.
validity_evidence: Accuracy vs real dashcam collision labels; closed-loop effect on NeuroNCAP.
bibtex: @misc{ma2025safevl, title={SafeVL: Driving Safety Evaluation via Meticulous Reasoning in Vision Language Models}, author={Ma, Yingzi and Cao, Yulong and Ding, Wenhao and Chen, Yuxiao and Weng, Xinshuo and Wang, Yan and Luo, Wenjie and Li, Boyi and Luo, Rachel and Veer, Sushant and Wang, Yue and Li, Xiaopeng and Sharma, Apoorva and Schmerling, Edward and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Xiao, Chaowei}, howpublished={NVIDIA ASPIRE preprint, submitted to ICRA 2026}, year={2025}, url={https://research.nvidia.com/labs/aspire/publication/ma.cao.etal.arxiv2025/}}
notes: No arXiv ID found; PDF via Google Drive on project page safevl.github.io; author list from NVIDIA page.

name: Pinocchio (faithfulness of embodied CoT)
modality: Reasoning traces of a driving VLA (Alpamayo-style) rated by humans and by a Gemini judge on observation grounding and stepwise coherence; learned critic used as RL reward; evaluated on held-out US/DE driving scenarios and synthetic counterfactuals.
what_it_measures: Whether verbalized reasoning of a driving VLA faithfully reflects its decisions, and whether faithfulness improves long-tail robustness.
size: 200-sample human study; 100 traces x 4 annotators for judge validation; ~20k DE and ~15k US held-out scenarios; 66 counterfactual scenes
reported_metrics: Gemini agrees with human majority 87-95%; human kappa 0.475-0.685; reasoning consistency 27.7% (SFT) to 61.4%; 1.6x causal-alignment gain on counterfactuals.
cost_evidence: Human annotation of 300 traces; large internal driving dataset.
validity_evidence: Human agreement numbers for the judge; inconsistent coupling between reasoning quality and trajectory improvement found.
bibtex: @article{foutter2026faithfulness, title={Do Vision-Language-Action Models Mean What They Say? On the Role of Faithfulness in Embodied Reasoning}, author={Foutter, Matthew and Cercola, Matteo and Wild, Lena and Wang, Yunshan and Li, Michelle and Gammelli, Daniele and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.04681}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04681}}
notes: Evaluation of reasoning, not of a safety outcome per se.

name: EUVS (Extrapolated Urban View Synthesis Benchmark)
modality: Neural rendering methods (3DGS/NeRF variants) trained on one traversal and tested on views from other traversals/vehicles/cameras (translation, rotation, both); scored by PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.
what_it_measures: How much sensor-simulation fidelity degrades when rendering viewpoints outside the training trajectory, i.e. how trustworthy reconstruction-based closed-loop simulators are.
size: 90,810 frames over 104 cases from nuPlan, Argoverse 2, MARS; 10 methods
reported_metrics: PSNR drops 23-40% from interpolated to extrapolated views; average degradation >25% across metrics.
cost_evidence: 300+ hours manual traversal selection, 800+ compute hours for COLMAP.
bibtex: @inproceedings{han2024euvs, title={Extrapolated Urban View Synthesis Benchmark}, author={Han, Xiangyu and Jia, Zhen and Li, Boyi and Wang, Yan and Ivanovic, Boris and You, Yurong and Liu, Lingjie and Wang, Yue and Pavone, Marco and Feng, Chen and Li, Yiming}, booktitle={IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05256}}
notes: Simulator-fidelity benchmark; safety_focus false but informs sim2real gap of AV validation.

name: CrashEvent / CrashLLM
modality: Crash reports converted to text; LLMs fine-tuned to predict crash type, severity, injuries; scored by F1.
what_it_measures: Whether LLMs can predict crash outcomes from contextual factors and support what-if traffic-safety analyses.
reported_metrics: Average F1 from 34.9% to 53.8%.
validity_evidence: Real crash labels as ground truth.
bibtex: @article{fan2024crashevent, title={Learning Traffic Crashes as Language: Datasets, Benchmarks, and What-if Causal Analyses}, author={Fan, Zhiwen and Wang, Pu and Zhao, Yang and Zhao, Yibo and Ivanovic, Boris and Wang, Zhangyang and Pavone, Marco and Yang, Hao Frank}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.10789}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10789}}
notes: Traffic-safety analytics rather than robot evaluation; adjacent.

name: Crash-report precedents for reasonable driving
modality: Crash narratives normalised to ego-centric language and indexed with driving logs; proposed actions adjudicated by retrieval and counterfactual reasoning; scored by recall of contextually preferred actions on nuScenes.
what_it_measures: Whether negative data (crash reports) improves calibration of driving decisions near safety boundaries.
size: nuScenes benchmark; crash report corpus size not stated
reported_metrics: Recall on preferred actions 24% to 53%.
bibtex: @article{patrikar2025negative, title={The Case for Negative Data: From Crash Reports to Counterfactuals for Reasonable Driving}, author={Patrikar, Jay and Sharma, Apoorva and Veer, Sushant and Li, Boyi and Scherer, Sebastian and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.18626}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18626}}
notes: Primarily a decision-making method; included because it defines a crash-grounded evaluation of action choices.

name: Task-aware risk estimation of perception failures
modality: Perception-monitor-flagged failures used to synthesise alternative plausible scenes; relative risk to the motion plan estimated with copulas (PAC bounds); evaluated on nuPlan; scored by F1/precision/recall of safety-maneuver triggering.
what_it_measures: Whether a perception error matters for the plan (system-level risk), and how well the estimator triggers safety maneuvers.
reported_metrics: Best F1, about double the best baseline; balanced recall/precision.
bibtex: @inproceedings{antonante2023taskaware, title={Task-Aware Risk Estimation of Perception Failures for Autonomous Vehicles}, author={Antonante, Pasquale and Veer, Sushant and Leung, Karen and Weng, Xinshuo and Carlone, Luca and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS)}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01870}}
notes: Runtime-monitor evaluation with clear protocol.

name: SPARQ (system-level perception-failure safety Q-network)
modality: Q-network scores whether a planner's proposed trajectory is safe given possible perception failures; recommends corrective plan; evaluated on nuPlan-Vegas; scored by accuracy/recall and runtime.
what_it_measures: Runtime safety assessment of motion plans against overlooked perception failures.
size: nuPlan-Vegas unseen test set (count not stated)
reported_metrics: 90% accuracy and recall at 42 Hz; compared with reachability baseline.
cost_evidence: Runs at 42 Hz on unseen test set; no hardware.
bibtex: @inproceedings{chakraborty2024sparq, title={System-Level Safety Monitoring and Recovery for Perception Failures in Autonomous Vehicles}, author={Chakraborty, Kaustav and Feng, Zeyuan and Veer, Sushant and Sharma, Apoorva and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Bansal, Somil}, booktitle={IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17630}}
notes: ICRA 2025 per NVIDIA page.

name: FORCE-OPT (predictor-based forward reachable sets for plan safety)
modality: Multimodal trajectory predictor distributions converted to conformally calibrated forward reachable sets; ego plan checked for intersection; Bayesian filter adapts conservativeness; evaluated on nuScenes with synthetic unsafe scenes; scored by coverage, FPR, FNR.
what_it_measures: Soundness and completeness of a plan-level safety monitor for end-to-end stacks.
size: nuScenes (~15 h); train Singapore, test Singapore (ID) and Boston (OOD)
reported_metrics: Coverage ~90%; FPR 8.6% (ID) / 5.2% (OOD); FNR 3.0% / 13.0%; 0.022 s per scenario; 7 baselines.
validity_evidence: Unsafe cases are synthetic edits of safe scenes; no real collisions.
bibtex: @article{chakraborty2025frs, title={Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans Using Trajectory Predictors as Forward Reachable Set Estimators}, author={Chakraborty, Kaustav and Feng, Zeyuan and Veer, Sushant and Sharma, Apoorva and Ding, Wenhao and Topan, Sever and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Bansal, Somil}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.22389}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22389}}
notes: Title literally 'Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans'; runtime monitor with reusable protocol.

name: Task-relevant failure detection for trajectory predictors
modality: Prediction errors propagated to planning cost; probabilistic runtime detector of harmful mispredictions with data-free calibration; scored by ROC AUC against other detectors.
what_it_measures: Detection of prediction failures that actually harm the plan, with bounds on false-positive and false-negative rates.
reported_metrics: Highest AUROC among compared detectors.
bibtex: @inproceedings{farid2022taskrelevant, title={Task-Relevant Failure Detection for Trajectory Predictors in Autonomous Vehicles}, author={Farid, Alec and Veer, Sushant and Ivanovic, Boris and Leung, Karen and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12380}}
notes: Related Bajcsy-group regret metric (arXiv 2403.04745) has no Pavone authorship.

name: Interaction-dynamics-aware perception safety zones
modality: Off-the-shelf nuScenes detector's false positives/negatives classified as safety-critical or not using a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety zone (ego-obstacle relative state grid); compared against circular-distance baseline.
what_it_measures: A safety-aware evaluation metric for obstacle detection: which perception errors matter.
size: nuScenes; 4644 false positives analysed; 40x40x20x15x15 state grid
reported_metrics: HJ zone flags 35 safety-critical FPs (0.75%) vs 305 (6.6%) for circular baseline, 8.7x reduction; 4.5 ms per object online, 228 s offline.
cost_evidence: 228 s offline compute, 28.8 MB memory, 4.5 ms per object.
bibtex: @inproceedings{topan2022perceptionzones, title={Interaction-Dynamics-Aware Perception Zones for Obstacle Detection Safety Evaluation}, author={Topan, Sever and Leung, Karen and Chen, Yuxiao and Tupekar, Pritish and Schmerling, Edward and Nilsson, Jonas and Cox, Michael and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12471}}
notes: Co-authored with NVIDIA safety team (Nilsson, Cox); kind=standard because it proposes an evaluation metric definition.

name: Maneuver-based perception safety zones
modality: Extension of perception safety zones: temporal-convolution decomposition by ego maneuver to shrink zone volume while retaining completeness; numerical experiments.
what_it_measures: Size of the perception safety-critical region conditioned on ego maneuver.
reported_metrics: Up to 76% zone-volume reduction while maintaining completeness.
bibtex: @article{topan2023maneuverzones, title={Refining Obstacle Perception Safety Zones via Maneuver-Based Decomposition}, author={Topan, Sever and Chen, Yuxiao and Schmerling, Edward and Leung, Karen and Nilsson, Jonas and Cox, Michael and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2308.06337}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.06337}}
notes: Incremental follow-up.

name: Rethinking Trajectory Forecasting Evaluation
modality: Argues accuracy-only forecasting metrics (ADE/FDE/NLL) are task-agnostic; proposes planning-aware weighting of prediction errors.
what_it_measures: Whether forecasting metrics reflect downstream planning outcomes.
reported_metrics: n/a (position paper with one example metric)
bibtex: @article{ivanovic2021rethinking, title={Rethinking Trajectory Forecasting Evaluation}, author={Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2107.10297}, year={2021}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10297}}
notes: Short position paper; superseded by 2110.03270.

name: Planning-aware prediction and detection metrics
modality: Prediction and detection outputs re-weighted by their effect on a downstream planner (via planner cost sensitivity); validated on an illustrative simulation and real AV data.
what_it_measures: Task-aware metrics for perception and prediction that better estimate closed-loop performance and outcome asymmetry.
reported_metrics: Task-aware metrics better estimate closed-loop performance than IoU/ADE (qualitative/relative results).
validity_evidence: Compared against closed-loop performance in simulation.
bibtex: @inproceedings{ivanovic2021planningaware, title={Injecting Planning-Awareness into Prediction and Detection Evaluation}, author={Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.03270}}
notes: Foundational for the group's 'task-aware evaluation' line.

name: Learning AV safety concepts from demonstrations
modality: Reasonable-behaviour assumptions learned from highway traffic-weaving demonstrations; safety concept synthesised via HOCBF / HJ reachability; used to evaluate real-world driving logs.
what_it_measures: Which logged interactions violate a data-derived safety concept; comparison with hand-designed concepts (e.g. RSS-like).
reported_metrics: Learned concept evaluates real driving logs; qualitative comparison to baselines.
bibtex: @inproceedings{leung2022safetyconcepts, title={Learning Autonomous Vehicle Safety Concepts from Demonstrations}, author={Leung, Karen and Veer, Sushant and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={American Control Conference (ACC)}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02761}}
notes: Venue inferred (ACC 2023) from ASL listing style; verify before citing venue.

name: Data-driven synthesis of AV safety concepts (HJ reachability)
modality: Embeds existing AV safety concepts (RSS etc.) in a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability framework to compare assumptions; proposes data-driven tailoring for responsibility and context.
what_it_measures: A common language for comparing and evaluating AV safety concepts.
reported_metrics: n/a
bibtex: @article{leung2021synthesis, title={Towards Data-Driven Synthesis of Autonomous Vehicle Safety Concepts}, author={Leung, Karen and Bajcsy, Andrea and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2107.14412}, year={2021}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.14412}}
notes: Co-authored with Andrea Bajcsy; conceptual, not an experimental evaluation.

name: Sample-efficient safety assurances via conformal prediction
modality: Warning system + simulator of robot/environment dynamics; conformal prediction tunes alert threshold to a provable false-negative rate; applied to a driver warning system and robotic grasping.
what_it_measures: Guaranteed false-negative rate of unsafe-situation warning systems using as few as 1/epsilon calibration samples.
reported_metrics: Empirically achieves guaranteed FNR with low FPR in both applications.
validity_evidence: Provable FNR under exchangeability; empirical confirmation.
bibtex: @article{luo2021conformal, title={Sample-Efficient Safety Assurances using Conformal Prediction}, author={Luo, Rachel and Zhao, Shengjia and Kuck, Jonathan and Ivanovic, Boris and Savarese, Silvio and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, journal={International Journal of Robotics Research}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14082}}
notes: IJRR 2023 per ASL page; directly about how many samples an assurance costs.

name: Online distribution-shift detection via recency prediction
modality: Streaming high-dimensional observations; detector with guaranteed false-positive rate; evaluated in simulation and hardware visual servoing.
what_it_measures: Detection speed and false-positive guarantee of a runtime distribution-shift monitor.
reported_metrics: Up to 11x faster detection than prior work; alerts issued before failure on hardware.
bibtex: @inproceedings{luo2022recency, title={Online Distribution Shift Detection via Recency Prediction}, author={Luo, Rachel and Sinha, Rohan and Sun, Yixiao and Hindy, Ali and Zhao, Shengjia and Savarese, Silvio and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09916}}
notes: Venue ICRA 2024 per arXiv comments; runtime-monitor evaluation.

name: Diagnostic runtime monitoring with martingales
modality: Multiple stochastic martingales run in parallel on streaming images to diagnose the cause of shift (sensor degradation, new environment, brightness); X-Plane taxiing and free-flyer hardware.
what_it_measures: Speed and accuracy of diagnosing distribution-shift cause so the right intervention can be applied.
size: X-Plane: 1000 taxi sequences (~30 images each); hardware: 9000 images from 30 episodes
reported_metrics: Detects cause up to 5x faster than conformal-martingale baseline (e.g. 14.9 vs 38.1 iterations).
bibtex: @inproceedings{hindy2024martingales, title={Diagnostic Runtime Monitoring with Martingales}, author={Hindy, Ali and Luo, Rachel and Banerjee, Somrita and Kuck, Jonathan and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.21748}}
notes: RSS 2025 per NVIDIA page.

name: Semantic anomaly detection with LLMs
modality: Scene converted to text via open-vocabulary detector (OWL-ViT); LLM (text-davinci-003) asked whether the scene is a semantic anomaly; CARLA driving FSM policy and Ravens manipulation policy; scored by TPR/TNR and agreement with humans.
what_it_measures: Whether an LLM monitor catches system-level semantic edge cases (stop signs on billboards, traffic lights on trucks) that component-level OOD detectors miss.
size: 69 handcrafted CARLA cases in 5 classes; 750 manipulation episodes
reported_metrics: Driving TPR 92% / TNR 78% (SCOD 30%, Mahalanobis 48%); manipulation detects 86% of semantic distractors vs 100% human.
validity_evidence: Agreement with human reasoning reported on manipulation distractors.
bibtex: @article{elhafsi2023semantic, title={Semantic Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models}, author={Elhafsi, Amine and Sinha, Rohan and Agia, Christopher and Schmerling, Edward and Nesnas, Issa and Pavone, Marco}, journal={Autonomous Robots}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11307}}
notes: Clear reusable test-case protocol.

name: AESOP (real-time LLM anomaly detection + reactive planning)
modality: Fast binary anomaly classifier in LLM embedding space triggers slow generative-LLM fallback selection inside an MPC with joint-feasibility branches; quadrotor and AV settings, sim and hardware.
what_it_measures: Anomaly-classification accuracy vs GPT-style reasoning and closed-loop safety of the fallback framework.
reported_metrics: Fast classifier outperforms autoregressive GPT reasoning even with small LMs.
bibtex: @inproceedings{sinha2024aesop, title={Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Reactive Planning with Large Language Models}, author={Sinha, Rohan and Elhafsi, Amine and Agia, Christopher and Foutter, Matthew and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS)}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08735}}
notes: Method paper; evaluation protocol partly reusable.

name: Vision-foundation-model embedding semantic anomaly detection
modality: Runtime images embedded with a vision foundation model (grid or instance-based) and compared to a nominal-scenario database; CARLA-simulated anomalies; compared with GPT-4o.
what_it_measures: Detection and localisation of semantic anomalies for driving.
reported_metrics: Instance-based method with filtering comparable to GPT-4o, with localisation.
bibtex: @inproceedings{ronecker2025vfm, title={Vision Foundation Model Embedding-Based Semantic Anomaly Detection}, author={Ronecker, Max Peter and Foutter, Matthew and Elhafsi, Amine and Gammelli, Daniele and Barakaiev, Ihor and Pavone, Marco and Watzenig, Daniel}, booktitle={ICRA 2025 Workshop on Safe VLMs}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07998}}

name: FORTRESS (OOD failure prevention via multimodal reasoning)
modality: Multimodal foundation models anticipate failure modes and fallback sets at low frequency; runtime monitor triggers fast fallback planning; safety-classification accuracy on synthetic benchmarks and real ANYmal data; quadrotor hardware urban navigation.
what_it_measures: Safety-classification accuracy and closed-loop planning success under OOD events.
size: synthetic benchmarks + real ANYmal data (counts not stated)
reported_metrics: Outperforms on-the-fly prompting of slow reasoning models in safety classification; improves safety and success on quadrotor hardware.
bibtex: @inproceedings{ganai2025fortress, title={Real-Time Out-of-Distribution Failure Prevention via Multi-Modal Reasoning}, author={Ganai, Milan and Sinha, Rohan and Agia, Christopher and Morton, Daniel and Di Lillo, Luigi and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10547}}
notes: Method paper with evaluation; CoRL 2025 per ASL page.

name: Sentinel (runtime monitoring of generative policies)
modality: Diffusion-policy rollouts monitored by statistical temporal action-consistency (STAC) plus VLM task-progress checks; sim (PushT, Close Box, Cover Object) and real mobile-manipulator Push Chair; scored by TPR/TNR/accuracy and detection latency.
what_it_measures: Failure-detection accuracy and latency for generative policies under OOD conditions.
size: 50 calibration rollouts per sim task; real: 10 calibration + 10 success + 10 failure episodes
reported_metrics: Combined detector 91-95% accuracy (TPR 93-100%, TNR 87-93%); 18% more failures than either detector alone; STAC 5-15 s, VLM ~21 s.
cost_evidence: Real mobile manipulator; small episode counts.
bibtex: @inproceedings{agia2024sentinel, title={Unpacking Failure Modes of Generative Policies: Runtime Monitoring of Consistency and Progress}, author={Agia, Christopher and Sinha, Rohan and Yang, Jingyun and Cao, Zi-ang and Antonova, Rika and Pavone, Marco and Bohg, Jeannette}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04640}}

name: A system-level view on OOD data in robotics
modality: Position paper: argues OOD should be judged by system-level competence rather than model-level detection; frames research questions on runtime monitoring, fallback and data lifecycle.
what_it_measures: n/a (conceptual framing of what an OOD-robustness evaluation should measure)
reported_metrics: n/a
bibtex: @article{sinha2022oodview, title={A System-Level View on Out-of-Distribution Data in Robotics}, author={Sinha, Rohan and Sharma, Apoorva and Banerjee, Somrita and Lew, Thomas and Luo, Rachel and Richards, Spencer M. and Sun, Yixiao and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2212.14020}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14020}}

name: System-level analysis of module uncertainty quantification
modality: Derives probabilistic specification on a module's uncertainty measure from a system spec and measures system input-output robustness; applied to a nuScenes driving stack (Trajectron++ + planner + MPC) and a Boeing runway-incursion detector/tracker.
what_it_measures: Whether a module's uncertainty estimate is useful to the system and how uncertainty-aware designs compare.
reported_metrics: Uncertainty-aware planners beat baseline on safety and holistic cost; histogram tracker miss rate 0.823 vs FPR 0.169.
bibtex: @inproceedings{deglurkar2024uq, title={System-Level Analysis of Module Uncertainty Quantification in the Autonomy Pipeline}, author={Deglurkar, Sampada and Shen, Haotian and Muthali, Anish and Pavone, Marco and Margineantu, Dragos and Karkus, Peter and Ivanovic, Boris and Tomlin, Claire J.}, booktitle={IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12019}}

name: AdvDO (realistic adversarial attacks on trajectory prediction)
modality: Optimisation-based attack with differentiable dynamics generates realistic adversarial agent histories; SOTA predictors benchmarked on general and planning-aware metrics; downstream AV simulated.
what_it_measures: Adversarial robustness of trajectory predictors and its downstream planning consequences.
reported_metrics: Prediction error up +50% (general) and +37% (planning-aware metrics); attacks cause off-road or collisions in simulation.
bibtex: @inproceedings{cao2022advdo, title={AdvDO: Realistic Adversarial Attacks for Trajectory Prediction}, author={Cao, Yulong and Xiao, Chaowei and Anandkumar, Anima and Xu, Danfei and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.08744}}

name: Robust trajectory prediction against adversarial attacks
modality: Adversarial training + domain-specific augmentation; robust model evaluated with a planner for accident rates.
what_it_measures: Robustness gains vs clean-data cost, and downstream collision/off-road rates.
reported_metrics: +46% on adversarial data at 3% clean-data cost; +21% adversarial / +9% clean vs prior robust methods; reduced severe accident rates with planner.
validity_evidence: Downstream planner accident rates in sim.
bibtex: @inproceedings{cao2022robust, title={Robust Trajectory Prediction against Adversarial Attacks}, author={Cao, Yulong and Xu, Danfei and Weng, Xinshuo and Mao, Zhuoqing and Anandkumar, Anima and Xiao, Chaowei and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00094}}

name: J-DAPT (robotic jailbreak detection)

reported_metrics: Detection accuracy near 100% with minimal overhead.
bibtex: @article{marchiori2025jdapt, title={Preventing Robotic Jailbreaking via Multimodal Domain Adaptation}, author={Marchiori, Francesco and Sinha, Rohan and Agia, Christopher and Robey, Alexander and Pappas, George J. and Conti, Mauro and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.23281}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23281}}

name: Semantic Lookout (maritime VLM hazard detection)

bibtex: @article{banerjee2022lifecycle, title={Data Lifecycle Management in Evolving Input Distributions for Learning-based Aerospace Applications}, author={Banerjee, Somrita and Sharma, Apoorva and Schmerling, Edward and Spolaor, Max and Nemerouf, Michael and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2209.06855}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06855}}
